entities.summary: Geography is the study of the terrestrial surface, the societies that inhabit it, and the territories, landscapes, places, or regions that form it when interacting with each other. This ancient discipline has its roots in the works of ancient Greeks such as Eratosthenes and Strabo, who sought to understand the Earth's shape and size. The development of geography was further shaped by the work of Italian Renaissance humanists, who emphasized the study of place and culture. In the modern era, geography has become a global discipline, incorporating insights from anthropology, sociology, and environmental science. Geographers today use a range of methods and technologies to study the complex relationships between people, places, and environments. The field has had a profound impact on our understanding of the world and our place within it, shaping fields such as urban planning, environmental policy, and disaster management. As the world becomes increasingly interconnected, the study of geography continues to play a vital role in helping us make sense of our globalized world.
